title: Craft Supply Swap Donation Days!
description:

title: Weekend Warrior Tennis (Saturdays)
description:
North Jersey Bowling, Volleyball, Tennis & More
Join us for friendly and sociable free rallies and possibly some informal matches for training and fun. We are beginner to intermediate levels but all are welcome. We don’t allow formal instruction on our group-reserved courts, although giving some quick tips is OK so long as you’re not holding up others waiting to play.

⛑️ **Clinic Matches:** If we have to rotate people in then we may play some clinic-style matches where everyone rotates in evenly. There is no holding the court via wins so everyone has a chance to play regardless of skill level.

🕊️ **Early Bird Start:** If you want to meet earlier than 9 AM (like 8 or 8:30) then please let us know by the day before and we’ll see who can join you (usually I can do earlier).

**🎾 Equipment:** Please bring your own racquet and water, as we don’t provide those. I always have some balls for at least one court, but feel free to bring your own in case we need to branch out over more than one court.

👟 **Court Priority:** Those who are signed up and show up by 9 AM will have top priority for court space. Those who show up later have second priority while those who are wait-listed will have third priority. This is only in the event that we have to rotate people in.

**🧯DISCLAIMER:** Courts are subject to availability and weather. If you make plans to attend please be prepared to cancel or adjust our location as needed. Furthermore, by attending you agree to be fully responsible for your own health and safety. Each person is responsible to take a break for rest and water at their own discretion.
source: Meetup: NJ Bowling, Volleyball, Tennis & More

title: 5 Week Course: The Work on Inadequacy (Timing Option A) Price - Sliding Scale
description:
The Mindful Stream
To celebrate 5 years of The Work Runs Free, Emrys has created The Work on Inadequacy. Over 5 weeks, we explore different ways the experience of inadequacy shows up in our lives, using The Work to investigate our experience.

Sign up form: [Click Here](https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSeQVso7QaCu9ubv5E_74f50c6vvp2nt7zx8zMWnlGkwaNIYMw/viewform?usp=preview)
Detailed Course Outline: [Click Here](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1eQYHU2jgRlNoO_XZDEjj08EhT8jeHk0h2zAOnEoglgM/edit?usp=sharing)

**Sliding Scale Price:** $120 — Accessible rate / $150 — Standard rate / $180 — Pay it forward

**Please note: the timing of Timing Option A will go back one hour from Sat Nov 7th onwards to 6AM PDT / 9AM EDT**

**Week 1 — I'm Not Good Enough:** The fundamental inadequacy story.
**Week 2 — Comparison:** Measuring ourselves against other people.
**Week 3 — I'm a Fraud / They'll Find Me Out:** Imposter feelings, competence and exposure.
**Week 4 — Being Loved, Accepted & Enough:** Inadequacy in relationships, belonging and being seen by others.
**Week 5 — Achievement & Where I Should Be:** Success, progress, potential and the feeling that we should be further along.

The course gently moves from the broader experience of inadequacy into increasingly specific areas where it can show up in our lives.

As we gently move into each topic, you are invited to become still and notice any stressful thought, belief or experience that arises through the inquiry, and to write it down — either on a notepad or in an electronic document.

Each session explores one stressful thought, or “one-liner,” using a format known as Popcorn Work. This is the same approach Emrys uses in his weekly *[The Work Runs Free](https://www.meetup.com/thework-runsfree/)* group. Everyone participates in their own inquiry, but there is no expectation to share. You are equally welcome to keep your inquiry entirely private, if that feels right for you.

The group is deliberately small, with a maximum of 10 participants, allowing us to explore together while each person remains connected to their own experience.

Please note that this is a paid course. In order to join you must register for the event (sign up form above). The Zoom link for this event will be sent around 24 hours after registration and payment has been made.

**To book a free introductory private session of The Work with Emrys, [click here](https://calendly.com/mindfulnesswithemrys/onehoursession)[.](https://mindfulnesswithemrys.business.site/)**

title: Theater League of Clifton Announces Auditions for “1776”
description:
The Theater League of Clifton will hold auditions for its upcoming production of “1776” on Tuesday, September 15; Wednesday, September 16; and Thursday, September 17, from 7:00 p.m. to 9:00 p.m. Callbacks by invitation may also be held Thursday, September 17. 
Auditions will be held at Living Hope, 303 Maplewood Ave., Clifton, NJ 07013.
Performances will be held November 13, 14 and 15 at the Wayne Community Center, 1 Pike Drive, Wayne, NJ.
The production will be directed by Maren Sugarman. 
With music and lyrics by Sherman Edwards and a book by Peter Stone, 1776 dramatizes the struggle within the Second Continental Congress to declare American independence. John Adams, Benjamin Franklin and Thomas Jefferson attempt to persuade a divided Congress to break with England while political, regional and personal conflicts threaten to derail the effort. 
Those auditioning should prepare 16 to 32 bars of a song and bring sheet music for the accompanist. A bluetooth speaker will be available if needed. Actors will also be asked to read selections from the script. Please bring a résumé and photo. 
For information on cast and characters, please visit https://www.theaterleagueofclifton.com/ or email theaterleagueofclifton@gmail.com or call (973)-928-7668 
Founded in 2005, the Theater League of Clifton is a nonprofit community organization dedicated to fostering an appreciation of the arts through theatrical performances while providing quality entertainment for all ages. The Theater League of Clifton welcomes volunteers in all aspects of performance and production. 
1776
Music and Lyrics by SHERMAN EDWARDS
Book by PETER STONE
Based on a concept by SHERMAN EDWARDS
Original Production Directed by PETER HUNT
Originally Produced on the Broadway Stage by STUART OSTROW
1776 is presented through special arrangement with Music Theatre International (MTI). All authorized performance materials are also supplied by MTI.

title: Ontelaunee to Reading Potpourri Hike
description:
Metrotrails: NJ, PA, NY Metropolitan Area Hiking and More!
Join us for this very interesting point to point hike between Ontelauee Lake and Reading.
I've selected another Pennsylvania hike instead of shifting areas this time because there may be structures demolished soon that we need to see before it happens.
After meeting in Reading at the Dollar General, we will shuttle with as few vehicles as possible to our start point.
There are several trails, and some abandoned roads along the lake. Some of it is an abandoned former road that had been used prior to the creation of the lake.
We'll weave around on the trail system in an indirect route, and then make our way onto some back roads, through school ball fields, and then south onto a closed road and past an historic bridge.
We will continued from here along a few more back roads to the Muhlenberg Rail Trail. We'll take that south just about to our end point.
Distance will be about sixteen miles.
If needed, contact me at 908 343 8374

title: Weekend Warrior Tennis (Sundays)
description:
North Jersey Bowling, Volleyball, Tennis & More
Join us for friendly and sociable free rallies and possibly some informal matches for training and fun. We are beginner to intermediate levels but all are welcome. We don’t allow formal instruction on our group-reserved courts, although giving some quick tips is OK so long as you’re not holding up others waiting to play.

⛑️ **Clinic Matches:** If we have to rotate people in then we may play some clinic-style matches where everyone rotates in evenly. There is no holding the court via wins so everyone has a chance to play regardless of skill level.

🕊️ **Early Bird Start:** If you want to meet earlier than 9 AM (like 8 or 8:30) then please let us know by the day before and we’ll see who can join you (usually I can do earlier).

**🎾 Equipment:** Please bring your own racquet and water, as we don’t provide those. I always have some balls for at least one court, but feel free to bring your own in case we need to branch out over more than one court.

👟 **Court Priority:** Those who are signed up and show up by 9 AM will have top priority for court space. Those who show up later have second priority while those who are wait-listed will have third priority. This is only in the event that we have to rotate people in.

**🧯DISCLAIMER:** Courts are subject to availability and weather. If you make plans to attend please be prepared to cancel or adjust our location as needed. Furthermore, by attending you agree to be fully responsible for your own health and safety. Each person is responsible to take a break for rest and water at their own discretion.

title: From Swastika to Jim Crow (2000): Screening and Discussion
location: Montclair Main - Auditorium, Montclair Public Library
description:
This is a free Adult School event. Registration is required.

Explore an influential, little-known chapter in the history of Black-Jewish relations in America. We'll be screening a documentary film, From Swastika to Jim Crow,  based on a book by the same title by Gabrielle Simon Edgcomb. It tells the story of German-Jewish refugees, who, expelled from their homeland by Hitler and the Nazis, found new lives and careers at historically Black colleges and universities in the American South, influencing a whole generation of Black students and professionals. After the screening, Dr. Lillie Johnson Edwards and Rabbi Julie Roth, will discuss the film's significance. Dr. Edwards is a Drew University Professor Emerita of History and African American Studies. Rabbi Roth leads Congregation Shomrei Emunah of Montclair, NJ.

This program is co-sponsored by Shomrei Emunah (https://shomrei.org/) and The Mark Montclair https://themarkmtc.org).

title: Classic Films Now: Network
description:
Run Time: 121 Minutes. Recommended for ages 18+ 
A nation distrusts its institutions. News has become spectacle. Ordinary people fight to matter. Welcome to 1976. 
Best Picture nominee about a mentally unstable news anchor who, after being told he’s to be fired, becomes a media superstar when he begins delivering nightly rants and threatens an on-air suicide for his final broadcast. Paddy Chayevsky’s script won an Oscar for Best Original Screenplay; Peter Firth received a posthumous Best Actor award as the unhinged newsman; and Faye Dunaway won Best Actress as a scheming network exec. 
 
Classic Films Now brings major works of cinema back to the big screen, films that not only defined their own time but continue to speak to ours. Each installment of the series gathers a group of landmark films curated around a theme, period, artist, or movement, inviting audiences to discover how the works connect with contemporary life. 
This fall, Classic Films Now kicks off with a three-film series devoted to 1976, a remarkable year in American cinema and a revealing moment in the nation’s cultural imagination. Released in the shadow of Watergate, Vietnam, urban crisis, and the Bicentennial, All the President’s Men, Network, and Rocky offer three sharply different portraits of American life at a time of great transition and uncertainty. 
Screenings will be introduced and hosted by Rafer Guzmán. Rafer writes about movies, music, and popular culture for Newsday. He has been a film critic for WNYC, a co-host of the independent podcast “Movie Therapy,” and a staff writer at The Wall Street Journal.

Performances will be held November 13, 14 and 15 at the Wayne Community Center, 1 Pike Drive, Wayne, NJ.
The production will be directed by Maren Sugarman. 
With music and lyrics by Sherman Edwards and a book by Peter Stone, 1776 dramatizes the struggle within the Second Continental Congress to declare American independence. John Adams, Benjamin Franklin and Thomas Jefferson attempt to persuade a divided Congress to break with England while political, regional and personal conflicts threaten to derail the effort. 
Those auditioning should prepare 16 to 32 bars of a song and bring sheet music for the accompanist. A bluetooth speaker will be available if needed. Actors will also be asked to read selections from the script. Please bring a résumé and photo. 
For information on cast and characters, please visit https://www.theaterleagueofclifton.com/ or email theaterleagueofclifton@gmail.com or call (973)-928-7668 
Founded in 2005, the Theater League of Clifton is a nonprofit community organization dedicated to fostering an appreciation of the arts through theatrical performances while providing quality entertainment for all ages. The Theater League of Clifton welcomes volunteers in all aspects of performance and production. 
1776
Music and Lyrics by SHERMAN EDWARDS
Book by PETER STONE
Based on a concept by SHERMAN EDWARDS
Original Production Directed by PETER HUNT

1776 is presented through special arrangement with Music Theatre International (MTI). All authorized performance materials are also supplied by MTI.

title: 2026 Class Gift Tabling - Information and Philanthropy Cord Pick-Up
description:
Each year, our graduating class participates in a proud Class Gift tradition where members of the class invest in the University by supporting areas of Montclair State University that are most important to them. We invite the Class of 2026 to come together to show your support!
All gifts to Montclair count! Make your gift to any area of campus you feel most passionate about – such as the Emergency Book Fund, The Red Hawk Pantry, your school or college, The Fund for Montclair State or athletic program.
Your gift will pay it forward for future Red Hawks and kick-start your philanthropic connection to Montclair.

Commemorate your class year! Make a gift of at least $20.26 and you’ll receive your customized philanthropy cord to wear over your commencement robe. 
For a gift of $40, celebrate this milestone with your family, friends and colleagues by having your message displayed on the screen at the Commencement you will be participating in, and receive a customized philanthropy cord.

Customized philanthropy cords will be available for pick-up:

Monday, October 26 from 3:00 – 5:00 p.m. in the Student Center Lobby
Thursday, November 2nd  from 2:00 – 4:00 p.m. in the Student Center Lobby
Tuesday, December 8 in the Student Center Lobby

Graduates can also arrange to pick up their philanthropy cords in the Overlook Corporate Center, 150 Clove Road, Little Falls, NJ during business hours, Monday through Friday, 8:30 a.m. – 4:30 p.m. Philanthropy cords can also be mailed to those who cannot pick it up. Please contact James Stewart, Associate Director of Annual Giving at stewartj@montclair.edu or 973-655-5328 to finalize options to get your cords for the Winter Commencement.
Every student has benefitted from donor generosity to areas of academic support, emergency funding for students and overall priorities to boost students’ success every day. title: Theater League of Clifton Announces Auditions for “1776”
description:
The Theater League of Clifton will hold auditions for its upcoming production of “1776” on Tuesday, September 15; Wednesday, September 16; and Thursday, September 17, from 7:00 p.m. to 9:00 p.m. Callbacks by invitation may also be held Thursday, September 17. 
Auditions will be held at Living Hope, 303 Maplewood Ave., Clifton, NJ 07013.
Performances will be held November 13, 14 and 15 at the Wayne Community Center, 1 Pike Drive, Wayne, NJ.
The production will be directed by Maren Sugarman. 
With music and lyrics by Sherman Edwards and a book by Peter Stone, 1776 dramatizes the struggle within the Second Continental Congress to declare American independence. John Adams, Benjamin Franklin and Thomas Jefferson attempt to persuade a divided Congress to break with England while political, regional and personal conflicts threaten to derail the effort. 
Those auditioning should prepare 16 to 32 bars of a song and bring sheet music for the accompanist. A bluetooth speaker will be available if needed. Actors will also be asked to read selections from the script. Please bring a résumé and photo. 
For information on cast and characters, please visit https://www.theaterleagueofclifton.com/ or email theaterleagueofclifton@gmail.com or call (973)-928-7668 
Founded in 2005, the Theater League of Clifton is a nonprofit community organization dedicated to fostering an appreciation of the arts through theatrical performances while providing quality entertainment for all ages. The Theater League of Clifton welcomes volunteers in all aspects of performance and production. 
1776
Music and Lyrics by SHERMAN EDWARDS
Book by PETER STONE
Based on a concept by SHERMAN EDWARDS
Original Production Directed by PETER HUNT
Originally Produced on the Broadway Stage by STUART OSTROW
1776 is presented through special arrangement with Music Theatre International (MTI). All authorized performance materials are also supplied by MTI.

description:
Registered to vote using your campus address and need a ride to the polls? Don’t sweat it—Civic and Voter Engagement has your back!
On Tuesday, November 3, 2026, the Office of Civic and Voter Engagement will provide FREE shuttle transportation for students registered to vote using their campus address. Whether you're voting for the first time or just need a convenient way to get to your polling location, we're here to help!
BE AT THE RED HAWK PARKING DECK BEFORE 2:00 PM!
Our FREE Election Day shuttle departs at 2:00 PM. Check your polling location, make your voting plan, and arrive on time!
Election Day Information


Election Day: Tuesday, November 3, 2026


Polling Hours: 6:00 AM – 8:00 PM


Shuttle Departure: 2:00 PM


Pickup Location: Outside the Red Hawk Parking Deck


Who Can Ride: Students registered to vote using their campus address


Polling Locations
St. George's Antiochian Orthodox Church237 Long Hill Road, Little Falls, NJ
For students registered at Blanton Hall, Dinallo Heights, Hawks Crossing, Machuga Heights, Sinatra Hall, and The Village.
School #5136 Valley Road, Clifton, NJ
For students registered at Stone Hall and Bohn Hall.
How the Shuttle Works
The shuttle will make a full loop between both polling locations, allowing students time to cast their ballots before returning to campus.


Depart from the Red Hawk Parking Deck at 2:00 PM.


Drop students off at St. George's Antiochian Orthodox Church.


Continue to School #5 in Clifton to drop off students.


Return to St. George's to pick up students who have finished voting.


Stop again at School #5 to pick up returning students.


Return to the Red Hawk Parking Deck.


CHECK YOUR POLLING PLACE BEFORE YOU GO!
Don't guess where you vote—verify your assigned polling location before Election Day!
Visit the official New Jersey Polling Place Search, enter your registered voting address, and click “Submit” to find your polling place.
https://voter.svrs.nj.gov/polling-place-search
PLEASE NOTE: You cannot vote at just any polling location. You MUST vote at the polling place assigned to you based on your voter registration information. Please verify your polling location before boarding the shuttle to ensure you are traveling to the correct location.
YOUR VOTE. YOUR VOICE. YOUR RIDE.
Don't let transportation stand between you and the ballot box!
CHECK YOUR POLLING PLACE. MAKE YOUR PLAN. BE AT THE RED HAWK PARKING DECK BY 2:00 PM ON NOVEMBER 3!
We've got the ride covered—now it's your turn to show up!

title: Library Speakers Consortium - Reclaiming Your Inner Wisdom: Sacred Indigenous Teachings with Asha Frost
description:
You must register here to attend:  https://libraryc.org/nutleypubliclibrary/217344



In a fast-paced world that often leaves us feeling overwhelmed and disconnected, true healing does not come from looking outward—it begins within. Join us for a transformative virtual conversation with Indigenous Medicine Woman Asha Frost as she explores her groundbreaking book, You Are the Medicine: 13 Indigenous Teachings to Connect to Your Inner Wisdom, Reclaim Your Power, and Heal.

The Medicine you have been searching for lives within you. Follow the path of the 13 Ojibwe Moons with Animal Spirits and Ancestors as your guides as you unlock your connection to your own unique, inherent healing power. Through storytelling, ceremonies, and Shamanic journeys, learn to apply ancient wisdom to your life in ways that are respectful and conscious of the stolen lands, lives, and traditions of Indigenous peoples.

Discover how to:

- Ground and root into your own lineage and meet your Ancestral guides.
- Practice self-care and rest on your journey.
- Return to Ancestral ways of cleansing and purifying.
- Trust and surrender so you can manifest and thrive.
- Release self-doubt, fear, disconnection, and insecurity.

Register now and take the first step toward recognizing and reclaiming your innate wisdom. 

About the Author: 

Asha Frost (she/her) is an Indigenous Medicine Woman and a member of the Chippewas of Nawash First Nation. She is from the Crane Clan, the totem of leadership, and believes in holding space from vision and heart. As an energy healer, homeopath, and mentor, Asha has guided thousands of people through profound and lasting transformation.

Impacted by generational trauma and colonization, Asha has been on a lifelong journey of reclamation. A lupus diagnosis sent her on a path of studying and practicing a multitude of energy Medicine modalities with many guides. She has blended this life experience with her innate gifts and the wisdom of her Ancestors. She loves sharing her Medicine in powerful ways through Ceremonies, teachings, and speaking events. Through this work, she loves seeing people reclaim their roots, find their healing wisdom, and rise into their power.

Asha lives on Anishinaabe, Huron-Wendat, and Haudenosaunee Territory, with her husband and two beautiful children, with whom she co-creates a better world for the seven generations to come.

title: The American Experiment: Information, Power, and Democracy: The First Amendment
description:
Join President Koppell for his first lecture in the American Experiment series, where he will discuss Information, Power, and Democracy: The First Amendment.
The First Amendment is the cornerstone of American democracy because it guarantees the fundamental freedoms required for citizens to govern themselves, including freedom of speech, freedom of the press, and freedom of assembly.  Citizens need access to open debate, diverse viewpoints, and accurate information in order to make informed decisions. These freedoms also protect unpopular and minority opinions and act as a check on the state from censoring speech or controlling what people learn, think, and say.  This lecture examines the foundational freedoms of the First Amendment and how they are applied to contemporary American democratic life, including: the impact of money on expression, the role of new media and corporate media, the role of the press in investigating and disseminating information, the right to protest as a form of assembly and expression, and the challenges posed by misinformation, disinformation, polarization, fragmented media audiences, and declining public trust. At its center is a fundamental question for American democracy: What are the inherent rights and responsibilities of freedom of expression in a democratic society?





Hosted by: Campus Activities, Civic & Voter Engagement

Additional Information can be found at: https://montclair.campuslabs.com/engage/event/12650840

title: 'On This Ground' St. Benedict's Prep Discussion Panel with Anthony DePalma
location: Montclair Main - Auditorium, Montclair Public Library
description:
This is an Adult School class. Click HERE to register.

"On This Ground" tells the remarkable story of a school that refused to die in a city that almost did. The school is St. Benedict's Prep, the city is Newark, and the extraordinary people who accomplished this are the Benedictine monks of Newark Abbey and the students they've taught for over 150 years. Joining author and longtime Montclair resident Anthony DePalma will be Anthony Badger, a member of the first class in the reimagined St. Benedict's in 1973, and Jared Boone, St. Benedict's class of 2013, who is now program partner for the Schumann Fund for New Jersey. Both men gave back to St. Benedict's by teaching there before moving on to community-based careers. Both lived in Newark during their time as students at St. Benedict's and witnessed the many ways in which the resilience of the monks and their school helped stabilize the city during its darkest days, including the 1967 civil disturbances and the recent pandemic shutdown. We'll go over important ways that other schools can learn from and adapt some of St. Benedict's winning ways.

title: Theater League of Clifton Announces Auditions for “1776”
description:
The Theater League of Clifton will hold auditions for its upcoming production of “1776” on Tuesday, September 15; Wednesday, September 16; and Thursday, September 17, from 7:00 p.m. to 9:00 p.m. Callbacks by invitation may also be held Thursday, September 17. 
Auditions will be held at Living Hope, 303 Maplewood Ave., Clifton, NJ 07013.
Performances will be held November 13, 14 and 15 at the Wayne Community Center, 1 Pike Drive, Wayne, NJ.
The production will be directed by Maren Sugarman. 
With music and lyrics by Sherman Edwards and a book by Peter Stone, 1776 dramatizes the struggle within the Second Continental Congress to declare American independence. John Adams, Benjamin Franklin and Thomas Jefferson attempt to persuade a divided Congress to break with England while political, regional and personal conflicts threaten to derail the effort. 
Those auditioning should prepare 16 to 32 bars of a song and bring sheet music for the accompanist. A bluetooth speaker will be available if needed. Actors will also be asked to read selections from the script. Please bring a résumé and photo. 
For information on cast and characters, please visit https://www.theaterleagueofclifton.com/ or email theaterleagueofclifton@gmail.com or call (973)-928-7668 
Founded in 2005, the Theater League of Clifton is a nonprofit community organization dedicated to fostering an appreciation of the arts through theatrical performances while providing quality entertainment for all ages. The Theater League of Clifton welcomes volunteers in all aspects of performance and production. 
1776
Music and Lyrics by SHERMAN EDWARDS
Book by PETER STONE
Based on a concept by SHERMAN EDWARDS
Original Production Directed by PETER HUNT
Originally Produced on the Broadway Stage by STUART OSTROW
1776 is presented through special arrangement with Music Theatre International (MTI). All authorized performance materials are also supplied by MTI.

title: 5 Week Course: The Work on Inadequacy (Timing Option A) Price - Sliding Scale
description:
The Mindful Stream
To celebrate 5 years of The Work Runs Free, Emrys has created The Work on Inadequacy. Over 5 weeks, we explore different ways the experience of inadequacy shows up in our lives, using The Work to investigate our experience.

Sign up form: [Click Here](https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSeQVso7QaCu9ubv5E_74f50c6vvp2nt7zx8zMWnlGkwaNIYMw/viewform?usp=preview)
Detailed Course Outline: [Click Here](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1eQYHU2jgRlNoO_XZDEjj08EhT8jeHk0h2zAOnEoglgM/edit?usp=sharing)

**Sliding Scale Price:** $120 — Accessible rate / $150 — Standard rate / $180 — Pay it forward

**Please note: the timing of Timing Option A will go back one hour from Sat Nov 7th onwards to 6AM PDT / 9AM EDT**

**Week 1 — I'm Not Good Enough:** The fundamental inadequacy story.
**Week 2 — Comparison:** Measuring ourselves against other people.
**Week 3 — I'm a Fraud / They'll Find Me Out:** Imposter feelings, competence and exposure.
**Week 4 — Being Loved, Accepted & Enough:** Inadequacy in relationships, belonging and being seen by others.
**Week 5 — Achievement & Where I Should Be:** Success, progress, potential and the feeling that we should be further along.

The course gently moves from the broader experience of inadequacy into increasingly specific areas where it can show up in our lives.

As we gently move into each topic, you are invited to become still and notice any stressful thought, belief or experience that arises through the inquiry, and to write it down — either on a notepad or in an electronic document.

Each session explores one stressful thought, or “one-liner,” using a format known as Popcorn Work. This is the same approach Emrys uses in his weekly *[The Work Runs Free](https://www.meetup.com/thework-runsfree/)* group. Everyone participates in their own inquiry, but there is no expectation to share. You are equally welcome to keep your inquiry entirely private, if that feels right for you.

The group is deliberately small, with a maximum of 10 participants, allowing us to explore together while each person remains connected to their own experience.

Please note that this is a paid course. In order to join you must register for the event (sign up form above). The Zoom link for this event will be sent around 24 hours after registration and payment has been made.

**To book a free introductory private session of The Work with Emrys, [click here](https://calendly.com/mindfulnesswithemrys/onehoursession)[.](https://mindfulnesswithemrys.business.site/)**

title: Simple Sitting Meditation (15 minutes)
description:
The Mindful Stream
In these sessions, I will be doing guided meditations where we simply sit and notice what arises.

There is no agenda and no plan for how these sessions unfold. I might start off simply by asking us to notice what is already present. By becoming aware of what’s going on in our heads and in our body.

Then, the meditation may take on a life of its own.

Our job is to simply be present to what arises. We may notice the mind moving and chattering about. Or we may notice that it’s completely silent.

The goal here, if there is one, is to simply let ourselves be as we are.

title: Women and Money Roundtable - How to Make Sense of Today's Financial Markets
description:
A virtual, lively, and informative discussion on today’s financial markets and how they might fit into your portfolio. 


Julia Strayer and Liz Maccarone will lead a lively and informative discussion on today’s financial markets and how they might fit into your portfolio.

This is a virtual program that takes place over Zoom. As the date approaches, you will receive an email with the Zoom link.

About the Presenters

Julia Strayer, CPWA®, CIMA®, CRPC® Senior Vice President, Wealth Management Advisor.  Prior to joining Merrill Lynch Wealth Management in 2000, Julia was a vice president and private banker for BankBoston’s Private Bank for 7 years, responsible for asset management and trust services. Previously, Julia worked in marketing for 9 years with Merrill. Julia has a BA from Ohio State University and an MBA from New York University’s Stern School of Business. Julia has appeared on the CNBC show “Power Lunch,” CBS “This Morning,” WGCH’s “Women in Business,” in addition to featured articles in USA Today.

Liz Maccarone, CRPC® Senior Financial Advisor.  Liz joined Merrill Lynch Wealth Management in 2012. Liz works closely with high-net-worth individuals and their families to create personalized and comprehensive strategies that support their goals, including investment management, retirement planning, liability management, and multigenerational planning. Liz values the importance of establishing and cultivating relationships with families including the next generation. Liz graduated from Fairfield University with a dual bachelor’s degree in Finance and Marketing. She began her career working at a boutique investment firm as a Business Development Associate, specializing in commodities and futures trading.

title: CXLD - Home Repair Essentials
location: Montclair - Montclair High School, Montclair Public Library
description:
This is a paid Adult School class. 

Learn the fundamentals of home repair in this practical, hands-on workshop taught by Robert Haas, instructor of the popular Woodworking 101 and Advanced Woodworking classes. Held at Montclair High School, this course gives participants a behind-the-walls look at how common home features are built and maintained.

During the class, instructor Rob Haas will construct two demonstration walls that include doors and a window, showing how these elements are installed and how typical wall structures are assembled. Participants will also learn how traditional double-hung windows operate and how they can be repaired, including basic glass pane replacement.

The workshop will also introduce the basics of residential wiring, demonstrating how outlets and lighting are installed and connected. Throughout the session, Robert will answer questions and offer guidance on a wide range of home repair topics.

Whether you're a homeowner looking to handle basic repairs yourself or simply curious about how things in your home work, this class provides practical knowledge you can use right away.

title: Theater League of Clifton Announces Auditions for “1776”
description:
The Theater League of Clifton will hold auditions for its upcoming production of “1776” on Tuesday, September 15; Wednesday, September 16; and Thursday, September 17, from 7:00 p.m. to 9:00 p.m. Callbacks by invitation may also be held Thursday, September 17. 
Auditions will be held at Living Hope, 303 Maplewood Ave., Clifton, NJ 07013.
Performances will be held November 13, 14 and 15 at the Wayne Community Center, 1 Pike Drive, Wayne, NJ.
The production will be directed by Maren Sugarman. 
With music and lyrics by Sherman Edwards and a book by Peter Stone, 1776 dramatizes the struggle within the Second Continental Congress to declare American independence. John Adams, Benjamin Franklin and Thomas Jefferson attempt to persuade a divided Congress to break with England while political, regional and personal conflicts threaten to derail the effort. 
Those auditioning should prepare 16 to 32 bars of a song and bring sheet music for the accompanist. A bluetooth speaker will be available if needed. Actors will also be asked to read selections from the script. Please bring a résumé and photo. 
For information on cast and characters, please visit https://www.theaterleagueofclifton.com/ or email theaterleagueofclifton@gmail.com or call (973)-928-7668 
Founded in 2005, the Theater League of Clifton is a nonprofit community organization dedicated to fostering an appreciation of the arts through theatrical performances while providing quality entertainment for all ages. The Theater League of Clifton welcomes volunteers in all aspects of performance and production. 
1776
Music and Lyrics by SHERMAN EDWARDS
Book by PETER STONE
Based on a concept by SHERMAN EDWARDS
Original Production Directed by PETER HUNT
Originally Produced on the Broadway Stage by STUART OSTROW
1776 is presented through special arrangement with Music Theatre International (MTI). All authorized performance materials are also supplied by MTI.

Virtual Buddy Read begins: Oct. 5
In-Person Meeting: Nov. 5

"I live in two worlds. One is a world of books. I’ve been a resident of Faulkner’s Yoknapatawpha County, hunted the white whale aboard the Pequod, fought alongside Napoleon, sailed a raft with Huck and Jim, committed absurdities with Ignatius J. Reilly, rode a sad train with Anna Karenina and strolled down Swann’s Way..."

Rory Gilmore's Book Club is not only for fans of Gilmore Girls, it's for anyone who wants to explore the classics and challenge themselves by reading directly from the Rory Gilmore Reading List. We'll meet every other month at the library with coffee and treats to discuss our chosen book (please feel free to bring your favorite coffee mug!). We'll also be chatting virtually along the way thanks to the reading app Fable! Once you register for our book club, an invite link will be sent and you can join the app, granting you the ability to comment forum-style on each chapter as well as vote for our next book. Our virtual buddy read will begin on October 5, but please feel free to join in at any time!

If virtual book clubs aren't your thing, you're also welcome to simply meet up in-person to discuss the book as a whole.

All are welcome! ♡

title: Working with Your Angels, Guides & Master Teachers by RoseMarie Rubinetti Cappiello
description:
Join the West Caldwell Public Library in welcoming Bergen County NJ Author RoseMarie Rubinetti Cappiello;  Intuitive/Medium/Healer, Hospice Trained Grief Volunteer, Ordained Spiritual Minister, Certified Hypnotherapist, Yoga Instructor, Reiki Attuned, BS Physical Education MSU and Author of Speaking From Spirit. 

EVENT WILL TAKE PLACE AT THE TOWN HALL (30 CLINTON RD, 2ND FLOOR)

Do you feel connected to Spirit, higher intelligence– a consciousness greater than you? Do you actively call on this source for support to help you in your day to day life? What if you could access this creative force in a tangible, practical and authoritative way? We will discuss this often under-utilized resource and how to work with it in a more conscious and powerful way. We will call on and build our connection to our unseen helpers—who are always helping us anyway whether we believe in them or not- and build our success teams for health and wellness and for financial support, guidance, success, assistance and structure. We will call on the relationship specialists and even the ones for career guidance and direction. Just as there are people with special gifts and skills on Earth that can assist us- Higher Consciousness/Heaven is filled with such guides, teachers, helpers and angels that have specialties too. Come meet the teams, build the teams and work with the behind the scenes helpers that work with you. When you work consciously with your spirit teams you will notice that life just seems to work out easier. Things start falling into place miraculously. Details get ironed out and things come together in a perfect way. You will always be in the right place at the right time, meeting the right people and opportunities and resources show up in unexpected ways. This class can be taken over and over again to gain even more insight, help and support from spirit. This is truly life changing information. Please bring a notebook and pen.

Trained by the best teachers from Arthur Findlay College in England, RoseMarie has highly developed psychic, mediumistic, intuitive, healing abilities. She has worked professionally as a Medium/Intuitive/Healer since 2000 and has connected many people to their loved ones in Spirit through thousands of private medium readings and platform medium demonstrations throughout the United States. Many people claim their lives change dramatically after having a reading with her and that the weight of grief and sadness significantly decreases.

In addition, she is a Spiritual Teacher who teaches online classes in psychic-spiritual development and conducts live classes in many venues across the country. Some topics covered are Telepathy, Dream Interpretation, Psychic Studies, Mediumship Development and Understanding the Soul and Spirit.

She is also a regressionist who does private and group healing work and Other Life Regression (often referred to as Past Life Regression).

Through her hospice training she often works with people and their families as they are getting ready to transition. She feels completely privileged and blessed to do this work.

Lastly, she is an adjunct professor at Montclair State University NJ where she teaches yoga in the physical education department.

title: Secrets, Lies, and Unforgettable Twists: A Conversation with E. Lockhart
description:
Join us for an exciting author talk with #1 New York Times bestselling author E. Lockhart as we reflect on her impressive body of work, including the literary sensation We Were Liars, and even gain an exclusive sneak peek into her shimmering new thriller, The Pools. 

Once, in a small New England town known for its hot springs, something terrible happened. Something that should have been a warning to stay away from the pools, if the stories were to be believed.

But no one is afraid of the water anymore, even if they should be.

When new girl Lexie meets golden boy Chester, their chemistry is undeniable. She’s running from a glittering life she won’t speak about. He’s hiding secrets of his own. Their connection feels bigger than both of them, despite their damage.

One frigid winter morning in that small New England town, five people go for a swim in the pools. Five people, including Chester. What happens there sends shock waves through the town, changing life as Lexie knows it forever.

Register now to step into the gripping, suspenseful worlds of E. Lockhart and ask questions live!

 

About the Author: 

Lockhart is the #1 New York Times bestselling author of the LIARS novels: We Were Liars, Family of Liars, and We Fell Apart. We Were Liars is also an original series on Prime Video. Her other books include Again Again, Genuine Fraud, and The Disreputable History of Frankie Landau-Banks. She has been a finalist for the Los Angeles Times Book Prize and the National Book Award and an honoree for the Printz Award. She lives in Brooklyn, New York.

title: Theater League of Clifton Announces Auditions for “1776”
description:
The Theater League of Clifton will hold auditions for its upcoming production of “1776” on Tuesday, September 15; Wednesday, September 16; and Thursday, September 17, from 7:00 p.m. to 9:00 p.m. Callbacks by invitation may also be held Thursday, September 17. 
Auditions will be held at Living Hope, 303 Maplewood Ave., Clifton, NJ 07013.
Performances will be held November 13, 14 and 15 at the Wayne Community Center, 1 Pike Drive, Wayne, NJ.
The production will be directed by Maren Sugarman. 
With music and lyrics by Sherman Edwards and a book by Peter Stone, 1776 dramatizes the struggle within the Second Continental Congress to declare American independence. John Adams, Benjamin Franklin and Thomas Jefferson attempt to persuade a divided Congress to break with England while political, regional and personal conflicts threaten to derail the effort. 
Those auditioning should prepare 16 to 32 bars of a song and bring sheet music for the accompanist. A bluetooth speaker will be available if needed. Actors will also be asked to read selections from the script. Please bring a résumé and photo. 
For information on cast and characters, please visit https://www.theaterleagueofclifton.com/ or email theaterleagueofclifton@gmail.com or call (973)-928-7668 
Founded in 2005, the Theater League of Clifton is a nonprofit community organization dedicated to fostering an appreciation of the arts through theatrical performances while providing quality entertainment for all ages. The Theater League of Clifton welcomes volunteers in all aspects of performance and production. 
1776
Music and Lyrics by SHERMAN EDWARDS
Book by PETER STONE
Based on a concept by SHERMAN EDWARDS
Original Production Directed by PETER HUNT
Originally Produced on the Broadway Stage by STUART OSTROW
1776 is presented through special arrangement with Music Theatre International (MTI). All authorized performance materials are also supplied by MTI.

title: 1st International Symposium of Latino Oral History
description:
Join us for the First International Symposium of Latino Oral History, “Listening as Resistance: Oral History, Memory and the Latino Experience” taking place virtually on November 6–7. This two-day symposium will bring together scholars, students, educators, writers, and community members to explore the power of oral history and Latino storytelling as tools for preserving lived experiences, amplifying voices, and challenging dominant historical narratives.

title: 🥾 Let's Hike!! at Garret Mountain
description:
Let's Walk!!
“Let’s Walk” turns **13 years** old this November! Join us for a small celebration in the parking lot after today’s hike.

Garret Mountain Yellow and White Loop Trail is a heavily trafficked loop trail located near Woodland Park, New Jersey that features a lake and is good for all skill levels. The trail offers a number of activity options and is best used from March until October.

**PLEASE ARRIVE 5 MINUTES EARLY SO WE CAN START ON TIME!**

We will hike a moderate 3 miles. This is **not** a paved trail, please do **not** wear sneakers.

We will meet in the **Auto Overlook** parking lot. It’s a one way, you will pass the equestrian, Lambert Tower before reaching the sign for AUTO OVERLOOK.

As always, we will go at a moderate pace and won’t leave anyone behind. But **please be considerate** of others if you don't think you will be able to hike at a moderate pace for the duration.

[https://www.google.com/maps/place/Parking+lot,+Paterson,+NJ+07503/@40.9057189,-74.1750062,17z/data=!3m1!4b1!4m6!3m5!1s0x89c2fdd38a2aa1a1:0x526711cb124756e2!8m2!3d40.905813!4d-74.1750982!16s%2Fg%2F11fx7w406f?hl=en-US&entry=ttu](https://www.google.com/maps/place/Parking+lot,+Paterson,+NJ+07503/@40.9057189,-74.1750062,17z/data=!3m1!4b1!4m6!3m5!1s0x89c2fdd38a2aa1a1:0x526711cb124756e2!8m2!3d40.905813!4d-74.1750982!16s%2Fg%2F11fx7w406f?hl=en-US&entry=ttu)

Rain or extreme weather will cancel the event.

Disclaimer: If you join us for a hike, please understand that you are responsible for your own preparedness and well-being and will hold no one else liable in case of injury or mishap.

title: [MILL Senior Friday] World of Film with Mark Phelan
description:
Join us on Fridays for a day full of events for Seniors with the MILL @ MPL! All events are free and open to the public. Registration is recommended unless otherwise noted.


The Red Violin (1998) | R

The intricate history of a beautiful antique violin is traced from its creation in Cremona, Italy, in 1681, where a legendary violin maker paints it with his dead wife's blood to keep her memory alive, to an auction house in modern-day Montreal, where it draws the eye of an expert appraiser. Over the years between, the violin travels through four different countries, where it has a profound impact on all those who own it.

ABOUT THE INSTRUCTOR
MARK PHELAN - I am a lifelong film fanatic who eats, breathes, sleeps and drinks movies. I have studied with Donald Spoto at the New School in NYC and have a BA and MA in Speech and Theatre from MSU. I have also worked as an actor and have directed several plays in local regional and community theaters, including the Whole Theatre in Montclair and the Paper Mill Playhouse in Millburn, NJ. I am currently working as an adjunct professor teaching, among other courses, Introduction to Cinema.

title: Theater League of Clifton Announces Auditions for “1776”
description:
The Theater League of Clifton will hold auditions for its upcoming production of “1776” on Tuesday, September 15; Wednesday, September 16; and Thursday, September 17, from 7:00 p.m. to 9:00 p.m. Callbacks by invitation may also be held Thursday, September 17. 
Auditions will be held at Living Hope, 303 Maplewood Ave., Clifton, NJ 07013.
Performances will be held November 13, 14 and 15 at the Wayne Community Center, 1 Pike Drive, Wayne, NJ.
The production will be directed by Maren Sugarman. 
With music and lyrics by Sherman Edwards and a book by Peter Stone, 1776 dramatizes the struggle within the Second Continental Congress to declare American independence. John Adams, Benjamin Franklin and Thomas Jefferson attempt to persuade a divided Congress to break with England while political, regional and personal conflicts threaten to derail the effort. 
Those auditioning should prepare 16 to 32 bars of a song and bring sheet music for the accompanist. A bluetooth speaker will be available if needed. Actors will also be asked to read selections from the script. Please bring a résumé and photo. 
For information on cast and characters, please visit https://www.theaterleagueofclifton.com/ or email theaterleagueofclifton@gmail.com or call (973)-928-7668 
Founded in 2005, the Theater League of Clifton is a nonprofit community organization dedicated to fostering an appreciation of the arts through theatrical performances while providing quality entertainment for all ages. The Theater League of Clifton welcomes volunteers in all aspects of performance and production. 
1776
Music and Lyrics by SHERMAN EDWARDS
Book by PETER STONE
Based on a concept by SHERMAN EDWARDS
Original Production Directed by PETER HUNT
Originally Produced on the Broadway Stage by STUART OSTROW
1776 is presented through special arrangement with Music Theatre International (MTI). All authorized performance materials are also supplied by MTI.

title: Bowling Night - Montvale
description:
North Jersey Bowling, Volleyball, Tennis & More
This is an event for casual bowling at Montvale Lanes, 14 W. Grand Ave. All are welcome for **two games, food and drinks**, and any post- or pre-game hang out. Show up anytime! Questions or comments? You can message Andy Milone on Meetup, or call/text him at **201-234-9609**.

\*\*\* Before bowling, we might stop by the Pizza Parlour, 6 S. Kinderkamack Road in Montvale, for a few slices. Post a comment on the event page to gauge interest. **After bowling, we'll definitely be heading to The Ridge Diner, 125 Kinderkamack Road in Park Ridge, at 10:15 p.m. for some food and/or drinks.** \*\*\*

About the group: People of all ages, backgrounds and abilities are welcome! We're not professionals and we're not in a league. In fact, we're a group of people who probably each won't score more than 100 points and will land more than our fair share of gutter balls. There's no pressure at all!!!! We're not here to analyze your form or technique.

More event details: You pay for your own games, food and drinks. Please bring cash. The alley does not accept card. But there is an ATM on site. **The** **cost per player is $18 for two games** **and bowling shoes.** If you have your own shoes, the cost is $12. Please try to bring exact change since Andy will have a limited amount of cash. If you bring a $20 bill and he doesn't have change, any remainder would just go toward the bowling alley tip.

Food and drinks (alcoholic and non-alcoholic) are available on site, plus tables and an alley bar to hang at during the event. There is a dart board and a few arcade games, as well.

**What do you do when you get there?** Find the group inside around the front desk. Look for a growing group of people! Call or text Andy Milone at 201-234-9609 if you can't find us. Once Andy secures the lanes, please pay him before getting your bowling shoes and heading to the lanes.

**Please know that it is possible we have to wait 20-40 minutes until lane(s) free up.** It's also possible that we may have to relocate or cancel that night if there's a long wait list upon arrival. Please keep that in mind if traveling from far away!

For those who don't have cars or are looking to avoid driving, the Montvale Train Station is only like a five-minute walk from the bowling alley and can be reached via the Pascack Valley Line. Last train leaves at 12:20 a.m. and heads toward Hoboken. (https://gmtma.org/wp-content/uploads/2011/11/rail_system_map.jpg)

Many thanks to Taylor, one of our group participants, for recommending Montvale Lanes! You can learn more at: www.montvalelanes.com.

Hope you'll join us for our 27th bowling event, or consider attending one of our volleyball, tennis or other activities -> www.meetup.com/north-jersey-bowling-soccer-volleyball

If interested in staying touch with group members or conversing about future events, feel free to inquire about our WhatsApp group chat.

title: 5 Week Course: The Work on Inadequacy (Timing Option A) Price - Sliding Scale
description:
The Mindful Stream
To celebrate 5 years of The Work Runs Free, Emrys has created The Work on Inadequacy. Over 5 weeks, we explore different ways the experience of inadequacy shows up in our lives, using The Work to investigate our experience.

Sign up form: [Click Here](https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSeQVso7QaCu9ubv5E_74f50c6vvp2nt7zx8zMWnlGkwaNIYMw/viewform?usp=preview)
Detailed Course Outline: [Click Here](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1eQYHU2jgRlNoO_XZDEjj08EhT8jeHk0h2zAOnEoglgM/edit?usp=sharing)

**Sliding Scale Price:** $120 — Accessible rate / $150 — Standard rate / $180 — Pay it forward

**Week 1 — I'm Not Good Enough:** The fundamental inadequacy story.
**Week 2 — Comparison:** Measuring ourselves against other people.
**Week 3 — I'm a Fraud / They'll Find Me Out:** Imposter feelings, competence and exposure.
**Week 4 — Being Loved, Accepted & Enough:** Inadequacy in relationships, belonging and being seen by others.
**Week 5 — Achievement & Where I Should Be:** Success, progress, potential and the feeling that we should be further along.

The course gently moves from the broader experience of inadequacy into increasingly specific areas where it can show up in our lives.

As we gently move into each topic, you are invited to become still and notice any stressful thought, belief or experience that arises through the inquiry, and to write it down — either on a notepad or in an electronic document.

Each session explores one stressful thought, or “one-liner,” using a format known as Popcorn Work. This is the same approach Emrys uses in his weekly *[The Work Runs Free](https://www.meetup.com/thework-runsfree/)* group. Everyone participates in their own inquiry, but there is no expectation to share. You are equally welcome to keep your inquiry entirely private, if that feels right for you.

The group is deliberately small, with a maximum of 10 participants, allowing us to explore together while each person remains connected to their own experience.

Please note that this is a paid course. In order to join you must register for the event (sign up form above). The Zoom link for this event will be sent around 24 hours after registration and payment has been made.

**To book a free introductory private session of The Work with Emrys, [click here](https://calendly.com/mindfulnesswithemrys/onehoursession)[.](https://mindfulnesswithemrys.business.site/)**

We don’t allow formal instruction on our group-reserved courts, although giving some quick tips is OK so long as you’re not holding up others waiting to play.

⛑️ **Clinic Matches:** If we have to rotate people in then we may play some clinic-style matches where everyone rotates in evenly. There is no holding the court via wins so everyone has a chance to play regardless of skill level.

🕊️ **Early Bird Start:** If you want to meet earlier than 9 AM (like 8 or 8:30) then please let us know by the day before and we’ll see who can join you (usually I can do earlier).

**🎾 Equipment:** Please bring your own racquet and water, as we don’t provide those. I always have some balls for at least one court, but feel free to bring your own in case we need to branch out over more than one court.

👟 **Court Priority:** Those who are signed up and show up by 9 AM will have top priority for court space. Those who show up later have second priority while those who are wait-listed will have third priority. This is only in the event that we have to rotate people in.

**🧯DISCLAIMER:** Courts are subject to availability and weather. If you make plans to attend please be prepared to cancel or adjust our location as needed. Furthermore, by attending you agree to be fully responsible for your own health and safety. Each person is responsible to take a break for rest and water at their own discretion.

title: PRE-ADVENT BEGINS
description: At Holy Spirit Verona we share in three weeks of "Pre-Advent" -- the three Sundays between All Saints and Advent 1. During this time we encourage you to take an intentional “pause” before the waiting and preparing of Advent. Advent used to be seven weeks, up until the 7th century, and there is a small movement within the Church to return to that (see theadventproject.org). Many of the scripture readings and prayers after All Saints give a hint or lean towards Advent, so Father Jerry says... why not just go there!Yes, we all know Father Jerry loves Advent. We are not bringing forth Christmas early like many retailers do, but rather allowing an intentional time to PAUSE before the all-consuming month of December. These three weeks of Pre-Advent, we hope, will bring forth a level of preparation and space during Advent which will make Christmas that much more meaningful. Our first experience of Pre-Advent was in 2018, so it's now officially a tradition! We get to see the blue hangings, which are symbolic of the Blessed Mother, for just a few extra weeks. Find some space these next three weeks to do something that will set you up well for the entrance of the Christ-child into our midst yet again. Join us as we prepare to prepare!
source: Church of the Holy Spirit Verona

description:

Join us for friendly and sociable free rallies and possibly some informal matches for training and fun. We are beginner to intermediate levels but all are welcome. We don’t allow formal instruction on our group-reserved courts, although giving some quick tips is OK so long as you’re not holding up others waiting to play.

⛑️ **Clinic Matches:** If we have to rotate people in then we may play some clinic-style matches where everyone rotates in evenly. There is no holding the court via wins so everyone has a chance to play regardless of skill level.

🕊️ **Early Bird Start:** If you want to meet earlier than 9 AM (like 8 or 8:30) then please let us know by the day before and we’ll see who can join you (usually I can do earlier).

**🎾 Equipment:** Please bring your own racquet and water, as we don’t provide those. I always have some balls for at least one court, but feel free to bring your own in case we need to branch out over more than one court.

👟 **Court Priority:** Those who are signed up and show up by 9 AM will have top priority for court space. Those who show up later have second priority while those who are wait-listed will have third priority. This is only in the event that we have to rotate people in.

**🧯DISCLAIMER:** Courts are subject to availability and weather. If you make plans to attend please be prepared to cancel or adjust our location as needed. Furthermore, by attending you agree to be fully responsible for your own health and safety. Each person is responsible to take a break for rest and water at their own discretion.

title: Classic Films Now: Rocky
description:
Run Time: 120 minutes, recommended for ages 11+ 
A nation distrusts its institutions. News has become spectacle. Ordinary people fight to matter. Welcome to 1976. 
A club fighter from Philadelphia who moonlights as a collector for a local mobster gets a shot at the big time when the heavyweight champion of the world gives him chance to fight for the belt on America’s bicentennial. 
 
Classic Films Now brings major works of cinema back to the big screen, films that not only defined their own time but continue to speak to ours. Each installment of the series gathers a group of landmark films curated around a theme, period, artist, or movement, inviting audiences to discover how the works connect with contemporary life. 
This fall, Classic Films Now kicks off with a three-film series devoted to 1976, a remarkable year in American cinema and a revealing moment in the nation’s cultural imagination. Released in the shadow of Watergate, Vietnam, urban crisis, and the Bicentennial, All the President’s Men, Network, and Rocky offer three sharply different portraits of American life at a time of great transition and uncertainty. 
Screenings will be introduced and hosted by Rafer Guzmán. Rafer writes about movies, music, and popular culture for Newsday. He has been a film critic for WNYC, a co-host of the independent podcast “Movie Therapy,” and a staff writer at The Wall Street Journal.

title: Kichwa Language Workshop Series
description:
LAIC (LATIN AMERICAN INDIGENOUS COLLABORATIVE) at CLaSE invites the Montclair State University community and the broader public to participate in our Kichwa Language & Culture Workshop Series, beginning Monday, September 14.
This 10-week workshop series offers participants the opportunity to learn Kichwa while exploring the language, culture, and traditions of Kichwa-speaking communities. Workshops are conducted in Spanish and Kichwa by our amazing and well known Kichwa community leaders - Atik Paguay and Fabian Muenala and are open to students, faculty, staff, families, and community members from outside the University. No previous knowledge of Kichwa is required.
Mondays, beginning September 145:30–7:30 p.m.Cole Hall, Room 14110-week series
We invite everyone interested in Indigenous languages and cultures to join us. Registration is required by contacting Dr. Calarota-Ninman at  calarotaa@montclair.edu

Hosted by: Center for Latino Heritage & Spanish Language Excellence

Community drum and chant circle rooted in Sufi prayer. 
Meets every other Monday:  November 9, 23, etc. 
Contribution: Sliding scale donation $20–$40 (no one will be turned away) 
This is a vibrant Community Drum and Chanting Circle, where we drum and chant from our hearts into the universe. This experience is open to absolutely everyone, regardless of background or belief system—all that’s required is an open heart and a willingness to connect through sound.  The term ‘lover’ in this context refers to seekers on the Sufi path who are longing for union with the divine energy.  You can think of this gathering as an expansion of the sema sufi meditations we used to offer.  It is looser in form, more focused on music, and does not necessarily involve whirling, although it is welcome if you are called to it. 
There is a rhythm older than thought. A pulse that moves beneath language, beneath belief, beneath the self that thinks it’s separate. The Mystics knew this. The Sufis practiced it in Majalis al-‘Ushshāq. The Assembly of Lovers. Not lovers of ideas. Not lovers of comfort. Lovers magnetized by the Beloved. Those who’ve tasted the Divine Honey and cannot forget. Whose hearts remember what the mind has been taught to ignore. This is a gathering for those who feel the pull. The Assembly of Lovers meets twice each month, a rhythm of remembrance. Each gathering deepens the last. The circle becomes a living pulse of devotion. If you have a drum, bring it. Medicine drums, frame drums, and ceremony drums are all welcome. The circle grows stronger when every heartbeat joins the rhythm. 
The Flow 
Opening (5 minutes)
We set intention. A short prayer to open the way. To align the heart toward what is Real. 
Chanting and Rhythm (30-40 minutes)
Using the Sufi Chants of the Heart as a guide (our vision is for the chants to grow to what the individuals in the circle are inspired to invoke), we share simple chants. The drum holds the pulse. The voice follows. The meanings are offered, not explained. 
Repetition is the technology. The heart softens through return. Through invoking the Divine until the one invoking dissolves. 
Silent Resting (5-10 minutes)
After the chanting, we sit. No guidance. No instruction. 
The echo of the words and rhythms settles. The heart rests in what was touched. 
Closing (5 minutes)
A prayer of Unity. Of Oneness. We complete the circle and return to silence. 
Gratitude for what was offered. For what was received. 
  
Who This Is For 
This is for those who’ve felt the pull and don’t know what to call it. 
For those tired of spiritual talk that never touches the ground. 
For those who suspect that the heart knows a language the mind cannot translate. 
For those who long. 
Not for something. Not for someone. 
Just longing itself. The flame that keeps you moving toward what you cannot name but cannot forget. 
Osama Janakat 
 
Osama studied Mathematics and Physics at Rutgers University, laying a foundation of analytical thinking that complements his creative pursuits. As a beat-maker and music producer, he explores the intriguing connections between music, philosophy, and spirituality. 
Born in Jordan with Circassian roots, Osama’s move to the US in 2004 sparked a journey of inner exploration and spiritual discovery. An avid student of the Sufi tradition, he continues to seek wisdom that bridges cultures and disciplines, finding harmony in the interplay of art and spirituality.

title: Beyond the Buzz: Managing AI’s Human, Cyber, and Legal Challenges
description:
Montclair Business Networking
AI is quickly becoming part of everyday business, and many small and mid-sized businesses are already experimenting with AI tools—often before formal policies or guidelines are in place. Leaders don’t need to slow innovation, but they do need practical guardrails to protect data, support employees, and ensure AI adoption is aligned with business goals.
This NJBIA Business Growth Roundtable will give business leaders a practical starting point for navigating AI responsibly. Experts in cybersecurity, law, privacy, and workforce leadership will share strategies for reducing risk, developing effective policies, and helping employees use AI thoughtfully and confidently.
What We’ll Cover

* Where informal AI use can create cybersecurity, privacy, compliance, and data protection risks

* What leaders should consider before employees use AI tools in their day-to-day work

* How practical policies, employee training, technical controls, and clear communication can work together

* What SMB leaders can do in the next 30 days to move AI adoption forward responsibly

Who Should Attend

* Solo professionals and small business owners already using or exploring AI tools

* Small and mid-sized business leaders developing practical AI guardrails

* Operations, HR, legal, IT, and cybersecurity decision-makers

* Leaders responsible for employee training, vendor management, or data protection

* Organizations looking to balance innovation with accountability, security, and employee readiness

title: Elvira Notari: Beyond Silence - Documentary Screening and Q&A with Director Valerio Ciriaci
description:
A DOCUMENTARY DIRECTED BY VALERIO CIRIACI (2025, Awen Films, 90mins)
Nov. 10 / 6:00 PM University Hall Conference Center, 7th Floor
Screening followed by an in-person conversation with the director 
Moderated by Teresa Fiore (Inserra Chair, Italian, CHSS) and Anthony Pemberton (Film, CCOM) with opening remarks by Mila Tenaglia (N.I.C.E.)
 
ELVIRA NOTARI: BEYOND SILENCE is a feature documentary chronicling the life and work of Elvira Notari (1875-1946), Italy's first woman film director. Despite directing hundreds of silent films that captivated audiences from Naples to New York, Elvira was relegated to the margins of film history for half a century. Her films, poised between realism and staged drama, were deeply rooted in Neapolitan folklore. A woman in a man’s world, her works were targeted by Fascist censorship yet found the embrace of audiences on both sides of the Atlantic. The documentary interweaves voices of those who celebrate her legacy today – from the experts who rediscovered her films to contemporary artists reimagining her vision through new works – to resurrect Elvira’s singular vision. More than a biography, Elvira Notari: Beyond Silence is a prismatic portrait of an artist who continues to inspire new creative pathways.
 
Select recognitions: Official Selection - Venice Classics at the 82nd Venice International Film Festival (World Premiere); Best Documentary, Globo d’Oro 2026; Shortlisted Best Documentary, David di Donatello 2026; Finalist – Documentary on Cinema, Performing Arts & Culture, Nastri d’Argento 2026.
A Parallelo 41 Produzioni and Awen Films co-production with Cinecittà. With support from the Italian Ministry of Culture, Film Commission Regione Campania, City of Naples, in collaboration with Casa Italiana Zerilli-Marimò at NYU and Archivio Audiovisivo del movimento operaio e democratico.
 
Valerio Ciriaci - director
Originally from Rome, Valerio moved to New York in 2011 to attend courses at New York Film Academy. In 2013 he co-founded Awen Films, a production company specializing in  independent documentaries with a focus on transnational and historical topics. As director, his filmography highlights include If Only I Were That Warrior (Globo d’Oro 2016, aired on Rai Storia); Mister Wonderland (‘Il Cinemino’ prize at Festival dei Popoli, aired on Rai, and PBS); and Stonebreakers (Honorable Mention, Audience Award, and the ‘Imperdibili’ prize at Festival dei Popoli), which has been screened over 100 times at leading cinemas and international cultural institutions. His latest feature, Elvira Notari: Beyond Silence, premiered at the 82nd Venice International Film Festival in the Classics section.
 
The event is co-organized and co-sponsored by NICE. (New Italian Cinema Events) and the Inserra Chair in Italian and Italian American Studies (Italian Program, Global Cultural Studies Department, College of the Humanities and Social Sciences), and the Animation, Film and Television program, College of Communication and Media).
 
The event is moderated by Prof. Teresa Fiore (Inserra Chair in Italian and Italian American Studies, Global Cultural Studies Dept., College of the Humanities and Social Sciences) and Prof. Anthony Pemberton (Animation, Film and Television Dept., College of Communication and Media) with opening remarks by Mila Tenaglia (Executive Director, N.I.C.E., an organization celebrating its 36th edition in the United States under the direction of its founder, Viviana del Bianco).

title: 5 Week Course: The Work on Inadequacy (Timing Option A) Price - Sliding Scale
description:
The Mindful Stream
To celebrate 5 years of The Work Runs Free, Emrys has created The Work on Inadequacy. Over 5 weeks, we explore different ways the experience of inadequacy shows up in our lives, using The Work to investigate our experience.

Sign up form: [Click Here](https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSeQVso7QaCu9ubv5E_74f50c6vvp2nt7zx8zMWnlGkwaNIYMw/viewform?usp=preview)
Detailed Course Outline: [Click Here](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1eQYHU2jgRlNoO_XZDEjj08EhT8jeHk0h2zAOnEoglgM/edit?usp=sharing)

**Sliding Scale Price:** $120 — Accessible rate / $150 — Standard rate / $180 — Pay it forward

**Please note: the timing of Timing Option A will go back one hour from Sat Nov 7th onwards to 6AM PDT / 9AM EDT**

**Week 1 — I'm Not Good Enough:** The fundamental inadequacy story.
**Week 2 — Comparison:** Measuring ourselves against other people.
**Week 3 — I'm a Fraud / They'll Find Me Out:** Imposter feelings, competence and exposure.
**Week 4 — Being Loved, Accepted & Enough:** Inadequacy in relationships, belonging and being seen by others.
**Week 5 — Achievement & Where I Should Be:** Success, progress, potential and the feeling that we should be further along.

The course gently moves from the broader experience of inadequacy into increasingly specific areas where it can show up in our lives.

As we gently move into each topic, you are invited to become still and notice any stressful thought, belief or experience that arises through the inquiry, and to write it down — either on a notepad or in an electronic document.

Each session explores one stressful thought, or “one-liner,” using a format known as Popcorn Work. This is the same approach Emrys uses in his weekly *[The Work Runs Free](https://www.meetup.com/thework-runsfree/)* group. Everyone participates in their own inquiry, but there is no expectation to share. You are equally welcome to keep your inquiry entirely private, if that feels right for you.

The group is deliberately small, with a maximum of 10 participants, allowing us to explore together while each person remains connected to their own experience.

Please note that this is a paid course. In order to join you must register for the event (sign up form above). The Zoom link for this event will be sent around 24 hours after registration and payment has been made.

**To book a free introductory private session of The Work with Emrys, [click here](https://calendly.com/mindfulnesswithemrys/onehoursession)[.](https://mindfulnesswithemrys.business.site/)**

title: Simple Sitting Meditation (15 minutes)
description:
The Mindful Stream
In these sessions, I will be doing guided meditations where we simply sit and notice what arises.

There is no agenda and no plan for how these sessions unfold. I might start off simply by asking us to notice what is already present. By becoming aware of what’s going on in our heads and in our body.

Then, the meditation may take on a life of its own.

Our job is to simply be present to what arises. We may notice the mind moving and chattering about. Or we may notice that it’s completely silent.

The goal here, if there is one, is to simply let ourselves be as we are.

title: Midday Meetup - Estate Planning
description:
**Midday MeetUp**   
A monthly gathering to make connections and learn together.  
12:30pm Catered Lunch (free)  
1:15pm  Featured Program   
  
**Topic** - Estate Planning: Four documents. Two tax systems. One integrated plan.  
**Presenter** - Linda F. Spiegel, Esq   
  
**Cost:** FREE or Suggested Donation of $10 per person to offset costs. (Bill My Account is only open to Shomrei Members)  
  
**RSVP:** Required so we know how much food to buy.  
https://shomrei.easyshul.com/events/6ad0ffd03e7684002567f097  
  
**\***Members should use their fob to access the building.  
  
**About the Program**  
Join Linda F. Spiegel for an overview of four essential estate planning documents: three that protect your wishes during your lifetime and one that guides the distribution of your estate after death. Learn how New Jersey’s inheritance tax and the federal estate tax fit into one integrated plan for your future.  
  
**About the Speaker**  
Linda F. Spiegel, Esq.is an Elder Care Planning mediator and works with families to help them with issues arising from aging relatives. When she is not mediating or arbitrating Ms. Spiegel works with individuals, couples and families in estate planning. She is also a divorce mediator assisting couples to reach an amicable resolution of their issues.  
  
Ms. Spiegel graduated from Barnard College, Columbia University and the Boston University School of Law. She is the Chair of the American Bar Association’s Senior Lawyers Division Alternate Dispute Resolution (ADR) Committee. In January. she was inducted into the National Academy of Distinguished Neutrals and is a recipient of a Joint Resolution of the Senate and General Assembly of the State of New Jersey for her work as a volunteer attorney with Project SARAH, Stop Abusive Relationships at Home.  
  
Additional_Dates_for_for_Midday_MeetUps: https://shomrei.org/calendar/midday-meetup-calendar

title: How Money Became God: Rethinking Wealth and Greed in Modern Society with Paul Vigna
description:
Join us for an eye-opening conversation with veteran journalist Paul Vigna as we examine his provocative book, The Almightier: How Money Became God, Greed Became Virtue, and Debt Became Sin, in which he explores the question: how did money go from a tool of commerce into the dominant faith of modern society? 

In The Almightier, Vigna takes readers on a sweeping historical journey from Renaissance Florence to today’s global financial markets, revealing how wealth accumulation evolved from a moral failing into an unspoken civic virtue. He uncovers the forgotten history of money, tracing the uneasy and often accidental alliance between wealth and religion as it developed from ancient city-states to today’s secular world, where religious devotion has receded and greed has stepped in to fill the void. 

Through engaging anecdotes, original research, and fresh perspectives on the causes of the many challenges we face today, Vigna makes a compelling argument that money has no power apart from the power we give it.

Whether you are interested in economic history, personal finance, or the hidden cultural forces shaping modern life, this talk is sure to pique your interest. 

Register today to learn more about how devotion to money has replaced religion as the foundation of our society.

 

About the Author: 

Paul Vigna is an author, journalist, editor and speaker, with a particular focus on capital markets and cryptocurrencies. He is the author of Guts: The Anatomy of The Walking Dead and coauthor of The Age of Cryptocurrency and The Truth Machine. For 25 years, he was a reporter and editor for Dow Jones Newswires and the Wall Street Journal, pioneering coverage of the cryptocurrency sector. He has appeared on CNN, CNBC, MSNBC, Fox, and PBS.

title: CANCELLED!! Everything Book Club,  "London Falling:" by Patrick Radden Keefe
location: Montclair Main - Tower Room, Montclair Public Library
description:
SEE SESSION 1 on Tuesday, Nov. 10. Goes with the Open Book / Open Mind program with Patrick Radden Keefe about "London Falling: A Mysterious Death in a Gilded City and a Family's Search for Truth" the following week on Tuesday, November 17! Tickets cost $40 and include a signed copy of the book. (If for any reason you can't afford a ticket, come talk to me.)

We'll talk about Keefe's conversation as well as "London Falling," a literary true crime investigation into the tragic death of a 19-year-old boy who, as it turns out, was masquerading as an oligarch's son in London's seamy underworld. 

“Gripping. . . . Keefe is a master at using true crime as a vehicle for exploring social and political pathologies.”
—NPR




Generally considered one of our greatest living non-fiction writers, PATRICK RADDEN KEEFE is a staff writer at The New Yorker and the author of The New York Times bestsellers "Rogues," "Empire of Pain" (winner of the 2021 Baillie Gifford Prize) and "Say Nothing," which received the National Book Critics Circle Award and was named one of the Twenty Best Books of the 21st Century by The New York Times Book Review. Keefe served as an Executive Producer on the award-winning FX series “Say Nothing,” based on his book.
